stories.headline: Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions
stories.summary: Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.
stories.body:
Next up on the calendar is the Bahrain Grand Prix, but there's a quirk -- the 16th round of the season is actually taking place almost 4,000 miles away in Malaysia.

George Russell closed the gap in the drivers' championship to 66 points from his Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli after taking his third win of the season at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Antonelli, who was hampered with all sorts of issues across the weekend, recovered from P16 to finish fifth.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the next race.

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

- George Russell warns 'pressure' is on Kimi Antonelli after 'most dominant weekend in my career'

- Lando Norris: Drivers should have 'one-race ban' after collision with Franco Colapinto at Azerbaijan GP

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia schedule
All times in BST

Friday, October 2

Practice One: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Saturday, October 3

Final Practice: 5.30 a.m. - 6.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 9 a.m. - 10 a.m.

Sunday, October 4

Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia: 8 a.m.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the Bahrain GP being hosted in Malaysia?
The Bahrain Grand Prix was cancelled in April due to the war in Iran, but it has now been rescheduled and will now be staged in Malaysia, meaning the race will remain on the F1 calendar.

There were several reasons why Malaysia was an obvious alternative, the main one being the way the calendar fell and the logistics involved.

It sits between the Azerbaijan Grand Prix which took place at the weekend, and will be followed by the Singapore Grand Prix on Oct. 11, resulting in a triple-header.

The last time the Malaysia Grand Prix held a race was in 2017. It spent 18 years on the calendar, so the infrastructure is there to be able to host a race with not much notice.

Sepang International Circuit

The Sepang is one of the circuits that is a complete test of car performance and driver ability. There is a mixture of long straights, heavy-braking zones and fast, flowing corners.

It is always one of the most humid races and due to the tropical weather, there can be heavy downpours of rain, changing the course of a race in an instant.

The combination of weather and the characteristics of the circuit always provide an exciting race and it is a driver and fan favourite as a result.

There is a tight hairpin at Turn 15, but either side are long straights which provide excellent overtaking opportunities.

Previous winners in Malaysia

2010: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2011: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2012: Fernando Alonso (Ferrari)

2013: Sebastian Vettel (Red Bull)

2014: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2015: Sebastian Vettel (Ferrari)

2016: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2017: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 1999

Laps: 56 laps of 5.5km

Lap record: 1:34.080 Sebastian Vettel (2017).

Most wins: Sebastian Vettel with four victories (2010-2011, 2013 and 2015). From the current grid, Fernando Alonso with three (2005, 2007 and 2012), Lewis Hamilton (2014), and Max Verstappen (2017) have each won here.

Most poles: Michael Schumacher (1999, 2000, 2001, 2002 and 2004) and Lewis Hamilton with five (2012, 2014, 2015, 2016 and 2017). From the current grid, Alonso has two poles (2003, 2005).

Weather forecast

The weather for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia is thundery showers and light winds through the weekend with highs of 33°C.

What happened in 2017?
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the race in dominant fashion after qualifying third on the grid. It was Lewis Hamilton's race to lose after he put his Mercedes on pole for the race which he's won once before, but he crossed the line in second.

Verstappen's teammate Daniel Ricciardo finished third, while Sebastian Vettel, who started from the back of the grid after suffering engine problems at Ferrari, managed to recover positions on the grid to finish fourth overall.

Vettel was 34 points behind Hamilton in the drivers' championship with five races to go.

Who will win this year?

There will be a slight element of the unknown heading into Malaysia given that over half of the grid have never raced here before. Teams and drivers have historic data to go off, but nobody will really know how the cars will perform until Friday's practice.

Russell didn't put a foot wrong last time out at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix and was incredibly quick all weekend and will carry that momentum into the next round.

Mercedes are also due to bring a major upgrade to Malaysia, while McLaren are expected to be strong around the high-speed circuit.

Red Bull brought major upgrades to Baku and were well in the fight, so rival teams will be keeping a close eye on Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar.

With rain expected, and it being one of the most popular circuits in F1, it could be an absolute thriller.

stories.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
stories.summary: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
stories.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

Bruno Fernandes

The Manchester United midfielder was left out of Portugal's squad for Sunday's game against Norway.

"He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United," Portugal boss Jorge Jesus said. "He really wanted to play against Wales."

Patrick Dorgu

The news for Manchester United fans who saw Fernandes absent worsened on Sunday when Dorgu was injured.

The left wing-back limped out of Denmark's match against Wales after 30 minutes.

Cody Gakpo

Liverpool forward Gakpo lasted only 17 minutes of the Netherlands' match against Serbia on Sunday. It means Liverpool are sweating over the fitness of Isak and Gakpo.

He looked in pain as he held the lower part of his right leg.

"It's his ankle, that's all I know," Netherlands boss Xavi Hernández said. "Tomorrow we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

stories.headline: Valkyries run away from Wings with franchise-record scoring, 3s
stories.summary: The Valkyries opened their postseason with one of the best offensive performances in franchise history Sunday.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- The Golden State Valkyries opened their playoff run with their best offensive performance of the season Sunday.

The Valkyries scored the most points in franchise history, beating the Dallas Wings 104-80 in Game 1 of the best-of-three first-round series. Golden State also tied its franchise record of 18 made 3-pointers in a game, the second-most 3s in a playoff game in WNBA history (the Aces hit 23 in Game 2 of the 2022 semifinals).

"It's really hard for teams to match up correctly or get into them if we're pushing [the pace] at a good rate," Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said.

Golden State became the first team in WNBA history to have six players hit multiple 3-pointers. Cecilia Zandalasini hit four 3s and finished with a game-high 22 points. Tiffany Hayes hit three 3-pointers and had 21 points. Gabby Williams, who finished with 20 points, Kayla Thornton, Kaitlyn Chen and Veronica Burton each hit two from beyond the arc.

The onslaught began in the second quarter, when the Valkyries outscored the Wings 37-11, including a 20-3 run over the last four minutes of the period.

"A 37-point quarter is insane work," Dallas guard Paige Bueckers said. "They got whatever they wanted."

Bueckers blamed the Valkyries' scoring barrage on the Wings not staying disciplined to their defensive game plan, which focused on limiting turnovers and guarding the 3-point line.

But it didn't matter whether the 3 was open or contested. The Valkyries made 12 contested 3s, the second most by a team over the past five postseasons. Only the Aces had more (15 in Game 2 of the 2022 semifinals).

Williams said the Valkyries played with a new level of offensive patience Sunday and were "able to be a lot more particular about what looks we're trying to get."

"Sometimes, we want to attack, attack, attack to the point where we're running into each other," Nakase said. "The discipline in spacing tonight, the patience in terms of when we attacked was really good ... and when that ball is moving ... it's key to our execution."

At practice Saturday, Nakase noted that the Valkyries' signature defense would help get the offense in a flow by making stops and allowing the team to push in transition.

The Valkyries relied on their physicality to find a rhythm Sunday.

"We're just getting stops and running and trying to tire them out," Williams said.

Bueckers agreed.

"It starts with their defense," she said. "They don't let their offense dictate their defense; it's the other way around. When they're flying around, getting stops, shots tend to go in more for them. It's tough on a team like that when you're never going to get their worst night defensively. They might miss shots, they might miss 3s, but they're always locked in defensively."

Bueckers said the Wings need to emulate that defensive intensity, adding that her team has a "nasty habit" of letting what happens on offense affect the defense.

"This is the playoffs, so it's really unacceptable," Bueckers said.

Bueckers finished with 21 points on 9-of-10 shooting, making her the first player in WNBA history to shoot 90% or better and score at least 20 points in a playoff debut. But she said every bucket was earned, not given. The Valkyries are OK with that.

"She's an excellent player -- one of the best in the league," Williams said. "As long as I can make [her shots] hard, where she has to really work for them, she will get tired. That's the goal. She's going to get them, but how can I wear her down?"

stories.headline: Bo Nix and Talanoa Hufanga lead the Broncos past the Rams 30-26 in a Sunday night thriller
stories.summary: — Bo Nix didn't flinch from his slow start and Talanoa Hufanga didn't lose faith after dropping two interceptions Sunday night.
stories.body:
DENVER -- — Bo Nix didn't flinch from his slow start and Talanoa Hufanga didn't lose faith after dropping two interceptions Sunday night.


Both bounced back in a big way, rallying the Denver Broncos past Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams 30-26 in the latest come-from-behind thriller that's become so common in the Mile High City.


Nix's keeper from inches outside the goal line with 47 seconds left capped a wild final five minutes that included a 66-yard pick-6 by Hufanga, a quick touchdown response by Los Angeles and a game-sealing second picked-off pass by Denver's do-everything safety.


“I actually had to have a pep talk with myself,” after dropping two interceptions earlier in the game, said Hufanga, who finished with a sack, a tackle for loss, a quarterback hit and three pass breakups to go with his pair of interceptions.


The Broncos (2-1) trailed 16-0 at halftime and went three-and-out to start the second half but rallied for a comeback, one-score win for the second straight week.


“In the huddle we feel a lot of belief that we've been there before and we have what it takes to go down against a really good defense and score points,” said Nix, who put the Broncos in front by reaching over the scrum with both hands squeezing the football.


Matthew Stafford, whose 17 comebacks in the last 2 minutes are the most by any active quarterback, quickly drove the Rams to the Denver 14, where he spiked the ball with 2 seconds left.


After false start moved the ball back to the 19, the Rams (1-2) sent out five receivers but Hufanga secured his second interception, this one in the end zone.


“Obviously a gutsy win,” Broncos coach Sean Payton said.


“I mean, it's a tough one,” Stafford said after the Rams, preseason favorites to represent the NFC in the Super Bowl, suffered a second loss in three weeks.


Hufanga's 66-yard pick-6 with 4:49 left gave Denver its first lead at 23-19. He jumped in front of running back Kyren Williams, cradled Stafford’s pass and weaved his way down the field, past the hard-charging QB and into the end zone.


“To be honest, Matt Stafford is a lot faster than you think,” Hufanga said. “I might be slow, but he's fast. I'll give him his credit because I had to cut back on that play.”


“Hufanga did a really nice job of fighting through the Y (receiver) and I left it a little bit back behind him,” Stafford lamented. "If I just dirt it, or whatever, we come away with three points. I’ll take myself trying to make those plays all day.”


Hufanga said he had told himself to stay patient for more opportunities to come after dropping two earlier potential interceptions of Stafford. “And man, two big plays.”


Just four plays later, however, Stafford hit Konata Mumpfield from 48 yards out when cornerback Riley Moss fell down, restoring the Rams' lead at 26-23.


Nix then drove Denver 65 yards in 10 plays with the aid of three defensive penalties and, with the ball nearly touching the goal line, leaped over the pile for the go-ahead TD. Nix had completions of 39 and 21 yards on that drive.


Cornerback Justin Wallace would have had his second interception of the night on that drive, but he was whistled for defensive pass interference on Pat Bryant on third-and-6 from the LA 11. That gave Denver a new set of downs at the 7.


“You try to be physical as a DB,” Rams safety Quentin Lake said. “Sometimes, you know, I think at the end of the day, as you know, the rules are the rules. Can’t be too handsy. It’s unfortunate.”


The Rams led 16-0 at halftime but it was tied going into the fourth after Nix threw a pair of touchdown passes and made two 2-point conversion throws: “We knew it was just a two-score game,” said Nix.


Harrison Mevis' fourth field goal, which followed an interception by Wallace, restored LA's lead at 19-16. He was also good from 36, 35 and 40 yards before halftime.


The Broncos cut their deficit in half on Nix's 5-yard strike to Bryant and 2-point conversion pass to Jaylen Waddle on a throw between the hands of Wallace midway through the third quarter. The Broncos tied it on another touchdown and 2-pointer. Nate Adkins caught an 8-yard throw from Nix, who found Bryant again to tie the game.


Stafford finished 30 for 55 for 390 yards. He threw 32 passes in the first half, the most of his career. With Puca Nacua out again with a hip injury, Davante Adams had seven receptions for 137 yards, giving him 15 catches for 332 yards over his last two games, the best such stretch of his career.


Injuries
Rams: CB Jaylen Watson (shoulder) got hurt just before halftime while guarding Courtland Sutton and was carted to the locker room from the sideline. LA lost two tight ends on its first touchdown drive, although Terrance Ferguson (ankle) returned on the Rams' next series. Also injured on the drive was Colby Parkinson (shoulder).


Broncos: Denver was without its Game 2 hero, rookie RB Jonah Coleman, who went on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain after his TD run secured the Broncos' 20-13 win over Jacksonville.


Up next
Rams: At Philadelphia next Sunday.


Broncos: Visit San Francisco next Sunday.

stories.headline: Struggling LAFC fires 1st-year coach Marc Dos Santos
stories.summary: LAFC fired head coach Marc Dos Santos on Sunday night, late in his disappointing first season in charge.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- LAFC fired head coach Marc Dos Santos on Sunday night, late in his disappointing first season in charge.

General manager John Thorrington announced the dismissal. LAFC didn't immediately name a replacement for Dos Santos, who was Thorrington's hand-picked successor to MLS Cup-winning coach Steve Cherundolo just nine months ago.

- Columbus stuns Miami late after Messi's free-kick golazo

"Marc has given a great deal to this club over the years, and we are grateful for his commitment, care and contributions to LAFC," Thorrington said in a statement.

LAFC undeniably has underachieved this season under Dos Santos, Cherundolo's assistant for four seasons and the former head coach of the Vancouver Whitecaps.

Despite a talented roster headlined by Son Heung-Min and Denis Bouanga, LAFC sits sixth in the Western Conference standings at 11-9-8 after winning just one of its past nine games across all competitions.

Dos Santos has incurred LAFC fans' ire for his static tactics and substitution plans, and his club has been booed at home by its normally supportive base.

Thorrington finally saw enough after LAFC lost 1-0 at FC Dallas on Saturday, dropping the club to 1-4-5 in MLS matches since July.

Dos Santos was only the third head coach in the history of LAFC, which began play as an MLS expansion club in 2018.

Bob Bradley immediately built a contender at the arena now known as BMO Stadium during his four seasons in charge, and Cherundolo led the club to the 2022 MLS title and the 2024 U.S. Open Cup before he resigned last year after four successful seasons, ostensibly to move back to Germany. But Cherundolo then agreed in July to coach the U.S. under-23 team through the 2028 Olympics.

Dos Santos' tenure started inauspiciously when Thorrington hired a head coach from within the organization for the second straight time, disappointing fans who wanted to see new tactics after Son's ballyhooed arrival last year.

LAFC started Dos Santos' MLS tenure impressively with a 3-0 win over defending champion Inter Miami in front of 75,673 fans at the Coliseum. But LAFC has struggled to make headway in the conference race, and it was bounced from the CONCACAF Champions League in May.

LAFC's next match isn't until Oct. 10 against Vancouver. The club has six games left in the regular season.

stories.headline: Islanders sign Logan Stanley to one-year contract
stories.summary: The Islanders have signed Logan Stanley to a one-year contract, adding the defenseman days before their season opener.
stories.body:
The New York Islanders have signed Logan Stanley to a one-year contract, adding the defenseman days before their season opener.

They added the 28-year-old left-handed shooter late in training camp after sending Kashawn Aitcheson and Isaiah George to their American Hockey League affiliate in Hamilton. George was considered a possibility to win a full-time roster spot at 22 after playing four games last season and 33 in 2024-25.

The No. 18 overall pick in 2016 by the Winnipeg Jets, Stanley was dealt to the Buffalo Sabres last season at the trade deadline. He finished the season with seven goals and 26 points, both career highs, while finishing a two-year, $2.5 million contract.

But Stanley struggled in the postseason and was scratched in Buffalo's final four games of a Round 2 loss to the Montreal Canadiens. He skated in eight playoff contests, accumulated 19 penalty minutes and finished with a minus-2 rating.

The Islanders, who have missed the playoffs the past two seasons and brought in Peter DeBoer as their new head coach, open the regular season Wednesday at the Toronto Maple Leafs.

A left-shot defenseman who is a native of Kitchener, Ontario, Stanley has international experience playing for Team Canada. In 2016, he played in the world junior championships, when Canada finished fourth.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Bulls trade Rob Dillingham to Hornets for Buddy Hield, cash
stories.summary: The Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash.
stories.body:
The Chicago Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Sunday.

Dillingham, the No. 8 pick in the 2024 NBA draft and still just 21 years old, was moved less than a year after landing in Chicago at the trade deadline last season. He appeared in 30 games for the Bulls, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

He could have a chance for a larger role in Charlotte, which traded longtime starting guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves earlier this offseason. Dillingham also joins the Hornets after Charlotte announced Friday that second-year guard Kon Knueppel has been sidelined with a hamstring injury.

The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the deal.

Hield spent less than a week with the Hornets, who acquired the veteran sharpshooter from the Atlanta Hawks for Dorian Finney-Smith. Hield, known as a positive and high-energy player, has history with Bulls executive vice president Bryson Graham from their time together in New Orleans.

Dillingham has one more year via a team option on his rookie contract before hitting restricted free agency in the summer of 2028. Hield has a player option worth around $10 million for the 2027-28 season.

stories.headline: Cleary may win Dally M from hospital bed after surgery
stories.summary: Nathan Cleary has had emergency surgery on his horror ankle injury, which could deny him the ability to accept the NRL's biggest individual award in person.
stories.body:
Nathan Cleary is set to miss out on claiming a long-awaiting Dally M Medal in person after the Penrith star underwent emergency surgery on his horrific ankle injury.

Cleary was rushed to hospital in Penrith's season-ending 22-14 loss to Newcastle on Sunday, after suffering a compound fracture and ankle dislocation.

Knights hooker Phoenix Crossland was on Monday referred straight to the judiciary over the incident, with the hip-drop tackle set to rule him out of the Grand Final.

Cleary has undergone the first round of surgery on his left leg, with the Panthers still unsure how long the four-time premiership-winning halfback will be sidelined for.

Another surgery is still required on Cleary's right foot, after Penrith revealed the No.7 had broken a bone in it during the week-one finals win over Sydney Roosters.

Those injuries will render Cleary unable to attend Wednesday night's Dally M ceremony at Barangaroo, where the playmaker is expected to win the top medal.

The Dally M is the one prize that has so far eluded Cleary throughout his illustrious career, but he is the strong frontrunner to claim this year's prize.

The two-time Clive Churchill Medalist held a healthy lead at the top of the leaderboard when votes went behind closed doors after round 12.

So gory was Cleary's injury, one Penrith official compared it to a gunshot wound when he returned to the sideline after the halfback was stretchered off on Sunday.

"It was really difficult to watch," Sydney Roosters veteran Daly Cherry-Evans said on Monday.

"I'm sending out all my love to him and his recovery process. I hope it goes really smoothly.

"I watch it through the lens sometimes as a dad, and watching his dad up in the coach's box, I just could not believe how he would be able to sit there, compose himself, and coach a side when his son has just had a pretty rough injury."

What Cleary's injury did prove is the kind of damage that must be done to remove one of Penrith's players from the field in a big match.

Dylan Edwards is also injured and suffered a suspected PCL rupture in the first half of Sunday's loss, but soldiered through.

He is now in doubt for the World Cup, with fellow fullback Reece Walsh also in a race against the clock for Australia's October 15 tournament opener against New Zealand.

Blaize Talagi ruptured his Achilles tendon in the second half, while Australia captain Isaah Yeo has admitted he may too have to pull out of the World Cup.

The Penrith lock had put off surgery on a ruptured pectoral muscle to play in the Panthers' finals series, but still needs to go under the knife.

"I don't know if I'll be available yet, I'll have to talk to the club as well because it will affect the start of next season if I was to prolong it," Yeo said.

"That's a conversation for probably later on next week with Ivan and the staff."

stories.headline: Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur vents frustration over Christian Horner's F1 job search
stories.summary: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has expressed frustration over the persistent speculation about his future at Maranello.
stories.body:
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has expressed frustration over the persistent speculation about his future at Maranello, which was only amplified earlier this week when former Red Bull boss Christian Horner stated his desire to take the top job at Ferrari.

Vasseur signed a multi-year contract to continue as Ferrari team principal last year, but it has done little to quieten rumours that his future beyond the end of this season could be in doubt.

Ferrari has won two races this year and is currently second in the constructors' standings -- albeit 160 points adrift of championship leaders Mercedes.

The Italian team has not scored a podium in the last five races, adding to the pressure on Vasseur, while Horner was quoted in an interview on Thursday saying the team principal role at Ferrari would be "the dream."

Horner was fired from his position as CEO and team principal at Red Bull last year but has made no secret of his desire to return to F1.

He stated previously that he would only return to F1 in a position that also includes a shareholding in a team, but in Thursday's interview said he would make an exception for Ferrari.

When asked about Horner's comments, Vasseur vented his frustration about the constant speculation around his future.

"We are not working in the perfect serenity," Vaseeur was quoted as saying by The Race following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. "For me firstly, but for everybody in the team.

"For the media, for 50% of the questions [to be] about this, I think it's a bit of a frustrating situation.

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

- Charles Leclerc admits Ferrari's rivals have taken 'big steps forwards': 'We must not lie to ourselves'

- George Russell warns 'pressure' is on Kimi Antonelli after 'most dominant weekend in my career'

"We are fighting for P2 in the championship, and at the end of the day, we are all speaking a lot about this, and even for the guys in the garage, to discuss about this, it's the best discussion that we can have.

"But it is what it is, it's not in my hands. Mr Horner is looking for a job -- that everybody knows -- everywhere.

"But what can I do? Just try to do my best to push the team, to rise them to be motivated, focus on what is better today.

"Each interview, 25 times a day, we are coming back to this."

He added: "But it is like it is. We have still seven races to go, and I will push until the last corner."

Following a sixth-place finish at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, Lewis Hamilton was asked by Sky Sports if he is still confident Ferrari is on a "good path" with Vasseur in charge, to which he simply responded: "Yes."

In a follow-up question Hamilton was asked if the team still had "good unity," and again he responded: "Yep."

Finally, when asked what the team can do over the remaining races, Hamilton said: "Keep trying."

stories.headline: 'Not my concern': Ex-Man City boss Mancini brushes off guilty reports
stories.summary: Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time in charge of the club.
stories.body:
Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time as manager.

A source confirmed to ESPN on Friday that City were expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of 115 charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

- Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Returning Mancini accepts fans' jeers as Italy beaten by Belgium

Among the alleged breaches cited by the Premier League in 2023 were that City had failed to provide "full details of manager remuneration in its relevant contracts with its manager" between 2009 and 2013, the period in which Mancini was in charge and delivered City's first title in 44 years.

According to German publication Der Spiegel, Mancini is said to have at one point earned £1.45 million in a basic salary and £1.75 million as a consultant for a team controlled by City owner Sheikh Mansour in Abu Dhabi.

But speaking at a news conference in Türkiye on Sunday, the now-Italy coach questioned the reported verdict and said it was a matter for the club, not him.

"It's not an issue that concerns me," he said in Bursa ahead of Monday's UEFA Nations League fixture. "It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years.

"Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

In a statement on Friday, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

In his own statement on Saturday, Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said "nothing has changed" regarding the case, adding "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

As well as the 2011-12 Premier League title, Mancini also led Man City to victory in the 2011 FA Cup final during his four seasons at the helm.

He returned to take charge of Italy for a second time this summer.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: NFL Week 3: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday's games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 3.
stories.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season featured shocking performances in the early window Sunday, including another turnover-filled afternoon by Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and a three-touchdown performance by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota also led the team to a huge upset over the Seahawks.

Elsewhere during the early window, the Steelers got the best of a shootout versus the Bengals. The Giants defeated the Titans without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, while the Browns won their second straight game.

The late window was filled with close games, with all four contests separated by a touchdown at the start of the fourth quarter. The Ravens-Cowboys matchup was the most exciting of the bunch in Rio de Janeiro, ending on a time-expiring, winning field goal by Baltimore's Tyler Loop. The Sunday night game was a classic, with the Broncos overcoming a 16-point halftime deficit to stun the Rams in the final minute in Denver.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

LAR-DEN | BAL-DAL

LV-NO | MIN-TB | ARI-SF

SEA-WSH | CAR-CLE | CIN-PIT

TEN-NYG | LAC-BUF | HOU-IND

NYJ-DET | NE-JAX | KC-MIA

Catch up on Thursday's game:

ATL-GB

Denver 30, L.A. Rams 26
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Broncos
Another wild comeback in the books, but can the Broncos continue to survive their chronic slow starts? The Broncos are 2-1 despite the first halves of their first three games being an exercise in offensive pain. The Broncos were held scoreless in the first two quarters Sunday night and have scored only 10 first-half points this season. The defense held Los Angeles to 1-of-3 in the red zone in the first two quarters, keeping the Broncos close enough for a second-half offensive surge. All-Pro safety Talanoa Hufanga had two interceptions, a pick-six and the game-sealing pick on the final play, but this penchant for close calls might come back to haunt Denver.

What to make of the QB performance: Bo Nix continues to show two personalities. He was out of sorts in the first half, completing 6 of 12 passes for 53 yards and nearly threw an interception. Same quarterback, different story in the second half. Nix once again bounced back despite a second-half interception. The Broncos scored on two of their first three possessions of the second half to tie the score after trailing by 16 points, and Nix led Denver to the winning score with 47 seconds left, capping a 65-yard drive with a 1-yard QB sneak for a touchdown. -- Jeff Legwold

Next game: at 49ers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Rams
Will Puka Nacua's return fix the Rams' red zone woes? The Rams' offense moved the ball well in the first half against the Broncos, gaining 273 yards, but struggled to convert in the red zone. The Rams were 1-of-4 in the red zone Sunday, with the lone score coming on a 5-yard touchdown pass from Matthew Stafford to tight end Tyler Higbee near the end of the first quarter. On the other two drives, the Rams had to settle for field goals. Nacua has missed the past two games but is expected to be back for Week 4 against the Eagles.

Key stat to know: In the first half, Davante Adams had four catches for 71 yards on five targets when matched up against Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II, whom Adams called "one of the best DBs in the league." Adams gained 71 yards in the first half, the most Surtain has given up before halftime in his career, according to ESPN Research. Adams finished the game with seven catches for 137 yards. -- Sarah Barshop

Next game: at Eagles (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Kyren Williams has had back-to-back games with 34 more rushing yards than expected and at least 15 fantasy points, strengthening his role as the Rams' primary back after Blake Corum totaled 22 carries in Weeks 1-2. Williams remains a weekly fantasy RB2, even with the Eagles up next. -- Cockcroft

Baltimore 34, Dallas 31
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Ravens
Did the Ravens exorcise their penchant for fourth-quarter collapses? Lamar Jackson and the Ravens gave an authoritative response to the "same old Ravens" narrative. Tyler Loop's 56-yard field goal with no time remaining lifted Baltimore to an improbable comeback. With seven seconds remaining, Jackson completed a 26-yard pass to wide receiver Zay Flowers, who was a game-time decision because of a hamstring injury. It was redemption for Loop, whose errant 44-yard field goal attempt ended Baltimore's playoff hopes last season. Over the past six seasons, the Ravens have lost an NFL-worst 15 games when leading through three quarters. But they found a way to win Sunday.

Stat to know: With two touchdowns, running back Derrick Henry became the oldest player (32 years, 166 days) in NFL history to score six touchdowns in the first three games of a season. His 34 career games with multiple rushing touchdowns are the most among active players -- 16 more than the next-closest players (Josh Jacobs and Jonathan Taylor with 18). -- Jamison Hensley

Next game: vs. Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Cowboys
Is this any different than the Cowboys' past two seasons? The Cowboys showed moxie to come back from an 11-point deficit, but ultimately, couldn't hold on. Why? A defense that was worn down and worn out. With 7:29 left, the offense had a chance to run down the clock but held the ball for only 1:44. Similar to 2024 and 2025, the Cowboys are 1-2 after two games. The comeback showed some fight, but now they won't get back to work until Tuesday due to traveling back from Brazil. Can Brian Schottenheimer's team make sure this isn't a repeat of the past two seasons, when they finished 7-10 and 7-9-1?

Key stat to know: The Cowboys are supposed to have a big-play offense, but Dak Prescott did not have a completion of more than 13 yards until the third quarter. On the go-ahead drive, he hit CeeDee Lamb for a 49-yard bomb from the Dallas 6-yard line. Before the completion to Lamb, Prescott had just one attempt of 20 or more yards and was attempting just 6.2 air yards per attempt. He averaged 7.4 in Weeks 1-2. -- Todd Archer

Next game: at Texans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Ravens backup TE Matthew Hibner caught both of his targets for 23 yards and a touchdown (10.3 fantasy points) on an end zone throw from Jackson. Hibner has run a total of only 23 routes over his first three games, but he projects as a potential insurance policy for starter Mark Andrews, who briefly left the game because of a hand injury. -- Bowen

Las Vegas 35, New Orleans 27
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Raiders
With Kirk Cousins playing well, will Fernando Mendoza have to wait longer than expected? The Raiders know Mendoza's time to be the starter is looming, but he might have to wait a little longer. Cousins has the Raiders at 3-0 and has played well. Against the Saints, Cousins completed 22 of 33 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns. He has thrown nine touchdowns in three games, and the team has fully embraced him as a leader. There's still no need to rush Mendoza on the field.

Key stat to know: Las Vegas scored 30-plus points in a game for the first time since its 63-21 win over the Chargers in Week 15 of 2023. The Raiders have scored at least 25 points in three straight contests. The Raiders scored more than 25 points only once during the 2025 campaign under former coach Pete Carroll.

Best quote from the locker room: "It's a 17-game season, so we can't be happy or satisfied with this win," Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said. "Put ourselves in a good position. We know what's coming to our place next week: the Chiefs. So we just take it one game at a time. That's how you win games."-- Ryan McFadden

Next game: vs. Chiefs (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Saints
What went wrong late for the Saints? Multiple turnovers were an issue in the second half. The Saints were playing backup left tackle Asim Richards because Kelvin Banks Jr. was on injured reserve, and Richards gave up a sack that led to a fumble and points for Las Vegas. Later, Richards was backed into Tyler Shough, who threw a wobbly interception as a result. The Raiders took the lead by scoring quickly afterward. The Saints had a chance to drive downfield and try to tie the score twice, but they turned the ball over -- again.

What to make of the QB performance: Shough was cooking until two fourth-quarter turnovers. The second-year QB showed an ability to move the offense at a level not seen in New Orleans in years. But Shough, who was making his 12th start, showed he still has some growing to do. Also, the Saints will have to get better about protecting their QB in key moments.

Best quote from the locker room: "Yeah, I don't know. I mean, there was just no flow to that game," Saints coach Kellen Moore commented on what Danny Stutsman should have done differently on a roughing the passer penalty that led to a Raiders second-quarter touchdown.-- Katherine Terrell

Next game: vs. Falcons (Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Forgive him for the two tough losses in three weeks, but the Saints' Shough has been outstanding operating in Kellen Moore's offense thus far. Shough has exceeded 22 fantasy points in all three games, is making good use of his receivers and is showing strong mobility. He has arrived as a matchup-dependent QB1. -- Cockcroft

Minnesota 23, Tampa Bay 16
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Vikings
Can WR Jordan Addison fill in for Justin Jefferson? Nope. And that's not intended to be a knock on Addison, who is a very talented WR2. But Jefferson, who left in the first quarter because of an ankle injury, is one of the best players in the NFL. Addison made several acrobatic catches, including a 30-yard reception along the sideline and a 41-yard touchdown. But to this point in his career, he has not been a receiver around whom opponents need to design their game plan.

What to make of the QB performance: Kyler Murray's first full game of his Vikings tenure was rocky to say the least. He found Addison on those two big plays, but otherwise, the Vikings couldn't move the ball after Jefferson departed. At one point, Murray completed only 2 of 15 passes. The Vikings barely had more first downs (nine) than punts (eight). -- Kevin Seifert

Next game: vs. Dolphins (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Buccaneers
Is there any hope of this getting better? The defense holding a Jefferson-less Vikings to six points in the second half gave the Bucs a chance, but what the offense is doing is unsustainable. Quarterback Baker Mayfield, who missed the final drive after injuring his thumb and finished 17-of-34 for 217 passing yards, was sacked six times, and the offense went just 2-of-17 on third down. That made it incredibly difficult to climb out of a 10-0 hole.

What to make of the QB performance: The Mayfield-to-Ted Hurst III connection showed improvement with a 40-yard touchdown in the first quarter, but a Luke Goedeke holding call wiped out Chris Godwin Jr.'s would-be score later on. And, of course, there was that fourth-quarter interception, which brought Mayfield's turnover total to five this season. -- Jenna Laine

Next game: vs. Packers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Addison's 20.0-fantasy-point performance aside, Buccaneers WR Emeka Egbuka's managers must hope that Mayfield's thumb injury doesn't sideline him long term. Egbuka hasn't hit his ceiling -- one he did often in the early stages of 2025 -- and he'd have a tougher time being a weekly WR2 with rookie Jalon Daniels as his QB. -- Cockcroft

San Francisco 36, Arizona 30
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

49ers
How much longer can the 49ers withstand all of the injuries? Perhaps no team in the league is more accustomed to fighting through significant injuries than the 49ers, but even they can withstand only so much. They eked out a win despite losing WR Mike Evans (ribs), LT Trent Williams (stinger) and LB Dre Greenlaw (quad) -- on top of the many players the 49ers were missing entering the game. The schedule gets tougher from here, starting with matchups against Denver and Seattle. Brock Purdy is playing as well as any quarterback in the league, and that effort has the Niners at 3-0, but Purdy must continue to perform for them to keep rolling.

Most surprising performance: Second-year WR Jordan Watkins had not played this season and entered Sunday's game with two catches for 26 yards in his career. But with Evans departing the game in the second quarter, Watkins got his opportunity. He had two catches for 60 yards, including a 34-yard catch to set up Eddy Pineiro's 57-yard field goal at the end of the first half.

Best quote from the locker room: Tight end George Kittle on the need of the 49ers' offense to carry the freight with so many injuries decimating the defense, especially on the line: "The NFL is hard to get wins in. With our offense, with coach Shanahan and with Brock Purdy at the helm, we need to put up points. And we have enough guys out there regardless of who's on the field, to score points, especially with Brock throwing the ball and Christian running it."-- Nick Wagoner

Next game: vs. Broncos (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Cardinals
How can the Cardinals' second-half offensive showing springboard them forward? Even in a loss, Arizona looked like a team that could score on anyone in the second half after scoring just six pints in the first half. Even though the 49ers were trying to keep the Cardinals' playmakers in front of them, they used a mix of short passes and the run to open medium and long passes. That turned a potential blowout into a close game.

Key stat to know: Eight. That's the number of penalties the Cardinals had in the first half, hampering offensive progress throughout the first two quarters. The Cardinals had just two in the second half, a telling difference . -- Josh Weinfuss

Next game: at Giants (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: If the 49ers' Evans misses time, managers should bump up TE George Kittle and WR Deebo Samuel Sr. as priority targets in the route tree. Plus, the receiving usage for RB Christian McCaffrey (flexed from the formation) could increase, which opens the door for rookie RB Kaelon Black to see more carries. -- Bowen

Washington 33, Seattle 31
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Commanders
How did this happen? Turnovers and an efficient offense. The Commanders forced three turnovers, leading to three touchdowns -- two by the offense and another on a pick-six by linebacker Kain Medrano. The offense capitalized on two short fields after a fumble and an interception, while quarterback Marcus Mariota did what was needed. He was smart with the ball, making quick throws and taking checkdowns to keep the chains moving. And he was aggressive when necessary, like on a tight-window throw to WR Trey Burks for his second touchdown. It was an unlikely win without quarterback Jayden Daniels, linebacker Frankie Luvu, tight end Chig Okonkwo, right guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Cross.

Trend to watch: Washington did not force any turnovers in its first two games, which continued an ugly trend: Only one team has forced fewer turnovers than the Commanders since 2024. But they harped on it all offseason, and the focus paid off Sunday. Can they sustain it? It helped that they played coverage much better than they did against Dallas in Week 2. But to get more, the front needs to generate more consistent pressure. It'll help when they get blitzing linebacker Frankie Luvu back soon from a groin injury. -- John Keim

Next game: vs. Colts in London (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET)

Seahawks
What was most concerning about Seattle's upset loss? The defending Super Bowl champions came into this game on a 12-game winning streak, with Sam Darnold back at quarterback, and as the much healthier team. There were plenty of reasons they lost as 8.5-point favorites, but a big one was their absence of a run game -- something they could have used in the rain. Seattle's tailbacks gained just 39 yards on 17 carries. Rookie Jadarian Price lost his second fumble in as many weeks to set up Washington's first touchdown. The Seahawks got away with turnovers last season because their defense and special teams were so good. But they didn't do enough to overcome three giveaways against Washington.

What to make of the QB performance: Darnold's return from the glute injury that sidelined him for most of the first two games was a mixed bag. With no run game, he carried the offense by completing 31 of 45 attempts for 379 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions -- one coming on a throw that was deflected at the line of scrimmage, while the other was a back-breaking pick-six in the fourth quarter. Two of Darnold's TD passes were to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but he spread the ball around more than Drew Lock did.

Next game: vs. Chargers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Best quote from the locker room: On his pick-six, Darnold was trying to find tight end AJ Barner, but defensive end Odafe Oweh kept him in the pocket, and Medrano jumped the short, play-action throw over the middle. "Just a bad decision," Darnold said. "The end did a good job of not letting me escape to the outside and I had to make a quick decision and I should have dirted it at his feet. ... I saw him. He made a really good play, but that's a ball I've got to throw away." -- Brady Henderson

Fantasy football takeaway: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin caught six of a team-high nine targets from Marcus Mariota, finishing with 77 yards and a touchdown (19.7 fantasy points). With this type of volume -- and clear on-field chemistry with Mariota -- McLaurin fits as a WR2/flex option for Week 4. -- Bowen

Cleveland 21, Carolina 18
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Browns
Is Deshaun Watson turning the corner? For the second straight week, Watson engineered a game-winning touchdown drive. This time, it helped turn around a slow start for the Browns' offense that lasted three quarters. Entering the fourth quarter, Watson was 10-for-21 for 67 yards and a touchdown. However, he has been at his best when the Browns have needed it the most. On the game-winning drive, Watson converted a pair of third downs, including his touchdown.

Key stat to know: Defensive tackle Mason Graham recorded his fourth sack in three games (two on Sunday against Bryce Young). That made him the first Browns player since Myles Garrett in 2019 to record a sack in the first three games of the season. Graham had a half-sack throughout all of last season as a rookie.

Best quote from the locker room: "We're playing for first place. Holy s---! Is that cool or what? Our guys are ready to rock and roll and we'll be good to go," coach Todd Monken exclaimed after Sunday's win. "But appreciate the fans and we're not perfect. We're not coaching or playing. We're going to fight like hell to get there, I promise." -- Daniel Oyefusi

Next game: vs. Steelers (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Panthers
Is this offensive line sustainable until Taylor Moton and Ikem Ekwonu return from their respective injuries? The Panthers have struggled to run the ball efficiently through three weeks. Carolina's ground attack was stifled Sunday, as running back Chuba Hubbard produced 18 yards on 10 carries in the first half; he still finished with 82 rushing yards on 19 carries. With left guard Damien Lewis forced from the game for a stretch, the line leaned on backup Corey Bullock, who didn't improve matters during his brief playing time. In addition, QB Bryce Young was sacked twice before halftime.

What to make of the QB performance: While Young led five scoring drives, his aerial attack was subdued by the Browns. He was erratic with a crowded pocket, and he benefited from a pair of roughing the passer penalties on the final drive of the first half to put points on the board. Young finished with 291 passing yards, a TD and an INT.

Best quote from the locker room: "I think we all just got to do a better job. I think we're just kind of -- I hate to say it -- one man off every time. That could be from me or anybody else," said Panthers right guard Rob Hunt of the team's run game struggles. "So we've just got to be on the same page. I think we've just got to click, and I think later in the game, it felt good and it looked good. We've got to start early. If we start early, it's a different ball game." -- Mike Kaye

Next game: vs. Lions (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Browns rookie WR Denzel Boston was a priority waiver wire add after catching a touchdown in each of his first two games. In Sunday's win, he caught only two of four targets for 41 yards (8.1 points). Boston has the explosive play ability to post a big number in the lineup, but he should be viewed as a boom/bust WR3 in a very inconsistent offense. -- Bowen

Pittsburgh 30, Cincinnati 27
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Steelers
How has CB Joey Porter Jr.'s absence impacted the Steelers? Porter was inactive for a third week in a row as he continues to "ramp up" amid his aggravated back injury and contentious contract situation. Bengals QB Joe Burrow picked on CB Asante Samuel Jr., eventually leading to rookie Daylen Everette replacing Samuel in the fourth quarter. Big-bodied receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase overpowered Samuel several times, including on Higgins' second-quarter touchdown, when the receiver boxed out the smaller Samuel. In the fourth quarter, the rookie was then part of a group responsible for a busted coverage that resulted in a Mike Gesicki touchdown.

Trend to watch: With Rico Dowdle out, running back Jaylen Warren played more than 90% of the offensive snaps -- a far cry from the balanced workload he carried with Dowdle in the first two weeks. With 17 carries for 127 yards, he showed Sunday that he's more than capable of carrying the load. It wasn't a perfect afternoon for Warren, though, as he got tripped up on the turf yards away from a breakaway touchdown late in the fourth quarter. -- Brooke Pryor

Best quote from the locker room: "It sucks that you have to have something like this happen after a loss," said LT Troy Fautanu on the offense's bounce-back performance. "Obviously you want to do this regardless if you win the week before or not, but sometimes you got to get punched in the face in order to learn."

Next game: at Browns (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Bengals
Are the Bengals playing well enough to be considered a serious contender? Sunday put a serious dent in that belief. After a good performance in all three phases against Houston, it was anything but that against the Steelers. Notably, the team had two bad special teams blunders -- a roughing the punter penalty and a muffed punt that ultimately led to 10 points. And Cincinnati's defense, while good in spots, gave up significant yardage after the catch, including on a late 47-yard reception by tight end Darnell Washington. The Steelers finished with 411 yards.

What to make of the QB performance: It was good up until the end. Burrow probably tried to do a bit too much trying to extend a play late and coughed up the ball with the Bengals driving for a potential tie or win. He completed his first 14 passes of the game and threw three touchdown passes, including a key fourth-down conversion that kept Cincinnati's hopes of winning alive. -- Ben Baby

Next game: vs. Jaguars (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Warren took on a volume role with Rico Dowdle out with a toe injury, scoring a season-high 20.6 fantasy points. If Dowdle has to sit again in Week 4, Warren can be played as a midtier RB2. -- Bowen

N.Y. Giants 12, Tennessee 7
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Giants
Did Jameis Winston do enough to inspire confidence as Giants QB? It wasn't perfect, but a win is a win. Winston did enough to help the Giants beat a struggling Titans team. His accuracy was off early, but he made some big plays throughout the game, especially on the opening drive of the second half. He finished 14-of-22 for 118 yards. It should be enough for him to remain the starter, and the Giants are still intent on adding another QB. Jimmy Garoppolo, J.J. McCarthy and Gardner Minshew are the most likely options.

Trend to watch: Running back Najee Harris' role increases. The veteran had four carries in his debut last week and nine Sunday for 52 yards. Harris jump-started the Giants' offense with six carries for 36 yards on their first drive of the second half. It should increase his playing time and role moving forward. Starter Cam Skattebo had 23 touches for 100 yards.

Best quote from the locker room: "That was a great win," Skattebo said. "A year ago, we lose that game 100%." -- Jordan Raanan

Next game: vs. Cardinals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Titans
Are the Titans playing like the worst team in the league? The Titans' offense was downright miserable for most of the game. Quarterback Cam Ward failed to see open receivers on multiple plays and missed Carnell Tate for what should have been an easy touchdown. They opened with five consecutive three-and-outs and finally got a first down late in the third quarter. The series of three-and-outs came after Chimere Dike fumbled the opening kickoff. It was a respectable effort by the defense, but Ward's inexplicable pass late in the fourth resulted in an interception and a Titans loss.

Trend to watch: Time of possession was an issue for the third game. At one point, the Giants held a 28:15 to 9:49 edge. The Titans managed to drive 91 yards in seven minutes late in the fourth quarter for their first points to help cut the deficit in time of possession and the overall score. The final drive, which ended in an interception, made it 34:26 to 25:34. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: at Ravens (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Giants WR Malik Nabers is struggling terribly with QB Jaxson Dart sidelined. Nabers' 7.6 fantasy points gives him two of the four worst fantasy scores of his career in the past two weeks. Nabers might have difficulty delivering even WR2 value without a QB upgrade. -- Cockcroft

Buffalo 24, L.A. Chargers 16
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bills
How did the Bills remain undefeated after committing five turnovers? Five turnovers, 10 penalties, two dropped interceptions and four sacks allowed. Quarterback Josh Allen's passer rating was barely north of 50. The Bills had no right to have kept this one close, but despite that the game never spun out of control. These battled-tested Bills somehow avoided spiraling or pressing. Give the defense its flowers, but the real impressive trend was the team's overall composure in the face of mistake after mistake to keep the win in reach.

Key stat to know: This was the first time the Bills won a game with a minus-four turnover differential since 1997. The opposing quarterback that afternoon was Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh. That was also the last time the Bills won any game in which they turned the ball over five times.

Best quote from the locker room: When asked if it felt like the Bills stole their win over the Chargers, Allen said it 100% did. "To be tied at halftime felt like a dream, to be honest," Allen said. -- Nick Suss

Next game: vs. Patriots (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Chargers
How concerning is Justin Herbert's start to the season? The defense tried its best to give Herbert and the offense a chance to win. Herbert -- who could have easily had three interceptions -- ended up throwing just one, and yet, the interception to C.J. Gardner-Johnson was a dagger. Herbert's play wasn't the only issue, as there were dropped passes and questionable playcalls. But ultimately, he hasn't looked like the superstar he was during the first six years of his career.

Most surprising performance: The Chargers' defense. Five turnovers typically means a win in the NFL. Somehow, it didn't on this day. Nevertheless, putting a lid on the league's best offense was encouraging. This is a unit that struggled against Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. So the Chargers should feel encouraged that their defense -- which has been the top unit the past two seasons -- is back. -- Kris Rhim

Next game: at Seahawks (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Is Chargers RB Omarion Hampton's grip on the primary running back role no longer ironclad? He barely edged Keaton Mitchell in snap share (42% to 36%) and total touches (15 to 11). Mitchell also had the better underlying metrics, hinting at more sharing moving forward. Add Mitchell, who is available in 84.4% of ESPN leagues. -- Cockcroft

Indianapolis 19, Houston 17
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Colts
Has the Colts' defense stopped the bleeding? The Colts entered this game ranked last in several major defensive categories, including a staggering 1,029 yards allowed in the first two weeks -- second most in NFL history. On Sunday, the missed assignments that led to wide-open receivers in the first two games and the flurry of missed tackles seemed to be mostly addressed. The Colts also took advantage of Houston's porous pass protection to consistently pressure Texans QB C.J. Stroud. Whether this was a one-week reprieve or the start of a trend, the Colts needed this.

What to make of the QB performance: Daniel Jones did not play smart in this game, as at least two of his three turnovers could be attributed to his own decisions. Jones' interception came when he threw a desperation pass while under pressure in field goal range. He also fumbled in the fourth quarter after not protecting the ball despite having multiple pass rushers converging on him. He did make some clutch throws on the game-winning drive. -- Stephen Holder

Next game: vs. Commanders in London (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET)

Texans
Is it time to panic on the Texans' 2026 season? It's trending that way. Even though the Texans' defense forced three turnovers (two in the second half) and had clutch plays from Stroud on their second-to-last drive to take the lead, it wasn't enough. Yes, the Texans started 0-3 last season and recovered, but that is not sustainable again. No team in NFL history has ever overcome 0-3 starts in back-to-back seasons, so expecting Houston to do that again is unrealistic.

Trend to watch: Houston's defense had zero turnovers coming into Week 3, but forced three, which gave them a chance to win. That's the type of playmaking defense Houston wants. And they're going to need it to dig themselves out of this hole. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: vs. Cowboys (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Colts WR Keenan Allen scored 18.3 fantasy points, stepping up as a short-route target over the middle while Alec Pierce (heel) heals. Daniel Jones' area of strength has come in the short game so far this season, so Allen shapes up as a matchup-dependent fantasy WR3 in the short term. -- Cockcroft

Detroit 31, N.Y. Jets 24
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Lions
Have the Lions fixed their defensive issues after rough start to season? After giving up 71 points through the first two weeks, Detroit shook up its secondary with Rock Ya-Sin serving a reserve role, while CB Roger McCreary started at outside cornerback alongside veteran D.J. Reed. Entering the game, the Lions were outgained by 191 total yards, fifth worst in the NFL, but second-year defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard refused to do any finger-pointing. Instead, he held a Monday meeting to dissect the struggles. The unit responded with a key takeaway in crunch time, but the defense still has major work to do.

Key stat to know: Jahmyr Gibbs finished with three total TDs, but his two rushing touchdowns helped him surpass Billy Sims (42) for the second-most rushing TDs (43) in franchise history -- trailing only Barry Sanders (99). Sanders was in attendance as part of the Lions' alumni homecoming. Gibbs put on a show in front of the Hall of Famer, finishing with 20 carries for 99 rushing yards and seven catches for 65 receiving yards. -- Eric Woodyard

Next game: at Panthers (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Jets
Why can't the Jets win close games? Another week, another crushing loss. The Jets had a chance to steal one in Motown, but their defense -- ranked No. 1 in yards allowed heading into the game -- imploded in crunch time. They let the Lions march 65 yards on four plays for the winning touchdown with 2:20 left in the fourth quarter, thanks to blown coverages on two pass plays. Then QB Geno Smith fumbled on the ensuing possession. Good teams rise up in the clutch; the Jets haven't mastered that yet. They blew a 10-point lead last week and lost in overtime. This week, a 14-point comeback wasn't enough.

Trend to watch: Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq has arrived. It took only three games for the first-round pick to establish himself as a versatile target. He caught seven passes for 105 yards, including a 24-yard touchdown on a diving play in the end zone. Sadiq now has a receiving TD and a rushing TD (Week 1) in his first three games.

Best quote from the locker room: Aaron Glenn on his close relationship with Dan Campbell: "I love him to death, I do. He's a huge part of how I've grown in this league. But this was a tough one for us. This is a tough one." -- Rich Cimini

Next game: at Bears (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Sadiq displayed his seam-stretching ability in a positive matchup versus the Lions' secondary, scoring a career-best 23.5 points. Available in over 65% of ESPN leagues, he should be added this week. But Sadiq should still be viewed only as a deeper league starter. -- Bowen

Jacksonville 35, New England 6
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Jaguars
Do the Jaguars even need Travis Hunter to play offense? After three weeks, Hunter has one catch and one carry. He hasn't touched the ball on offense since the opener. Hunter played five offensive snaps Sunday, giving him 16 for the season. But the Jaguars have scored 82 points, rookie WR Josh Cameron has emerged, and QB Trevor Lawrence is having success spreading the ball around. The run game cranked up against New England, too (135 yards). Why force Hunter on the field if the offense is rolling without him?

Most surprising performance: The Jaguars gave Cameron a bigger role in Week 3, and he delivered with a touchdown catch (second on three catches this season) and a 42-yard kickoff return. Through three quarters versus the Patriots, he had nearly as many snaps on offense (16) as Brian Thomas Jr. (21) -- an indication that more work could be ahead as the season progresses.

Best quote from the locker room: Hunter on his end zone interception: "I know [Maye] tried me a couple times, so I was just in there saying, 'I'm getting too close to the ball. I got to get me one.' So we just continued to just do what the coaches schemed up for us and we just played our best part of it." -- Michael DiRocco

Next game: at Bengals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Patriots
What can the Patriots do to get Drake Maye back on track? Maye's 2026 woes continued with his 10th game of multiple turnovers (tied for most in NFL since 2024). The end zone interception just before halftime, on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, was a shocking decision as WR Efton Chism III was tightly covered by Travis Hunter. It was a play similar to Maye's miscue in the season-opening loss at Seattle. In the first half, Maye was pressured 11 times -- his most before halftime in his career -- and went 2-of-7 with an interception and two sacks, per ESPN Research.

Trend to watch: Offensive line injuries. Veteran Greg Van Roten, who started at right guard in place of Mike Onwenu (broken ankle), didn't return after leaving the game in the second quarter (thigh). Walter Rouse, who was acquired in a trade with the Vikings in August, took over for Van Roten.

Best quote from the locker room: Maye on the biggest difference from last season: "I think it's getting out of my own way. These mistakes that I'm making personally are really [not] them beating us, it's me beating myself. ... This league will humble you quick." -- Mike Reiss

Next game: at Bills (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Though Chris Rodriguez Jr. scored, Bhayshul Tuten continued to flash his elite speed, scoring 17.0 fantasy points on 17 touches. Tuten's 48% snap share and usage offer encouragement that he can be a weekly fantasy RB2. (And, for what it's worth, sit Maye next week at Buffalo. Please.) -- Cockcroft

Kansas City 24, Miami 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Chiefs
Despite winning, should the Chiefs be concerned about their pass rush? Entering Week 3, no NFL QB had been sacked more than Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (nine). The fact that the Chiefs couldn't pressure him while not blitzing was similar to the pass-rush struggles of last season, when defensive tackle Chris Jones was the lone major presence. On Sunday, defensive end George Karlaftis was the lone defender to record a hit on Willis. The Chiefs won't beat better opponents with a similar performance. The Chiefs also didn't sack Colts quarterback Daniel Jones last week -- and that game ended in overtime.

Stat to know: Running back Kenneth Walker III is the first player to have two games with a rushing and receiving touchdown within his team's first three games of a season since 2017, when former running back Todd Gurley was a member of the Rams. Walker is also the first player in Chiefs history to accomplish the feat. -- Nate Taylor

Next game: at Raiders (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Dolphins
Have the Dolphins begun to turn the page on both sides of the ball? On defense, absolutely. The Dolphins kept the game in front of them, forced turnovers and rallied after an ugly first two drives. Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez recorded his first career takeaway and looked like a future star. The Chiefs' offense made plenty of mistakes, but Miami flew to the ball and limited explosives for the most part. Meanwhile, the Dolphins' passing game looked sharper than it has all season, but they struggled to run the ball after De'Von Achane was injured on the opening drive. We will see if Miami can build on this next week.

What to make of the QB performance: Willis completed 20 of 36 passes for 210 yards in possibly his best performance of the season. Unlike his previous two games, Willis made quicker decisions with the football and was far more willing to take off if receivers weren't open. That being said, his accuracy waned at times, and he missed a few deep shots. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Next game: at Vikings (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Dolphins RB Ollie Gordon II played 83% of the offensive snaps after Achane's injury, recording 20 touches and 14.5 fantasy points. The Dolphins would probably activate Jaylen Wright for depth next week, but Gordon should be a priority pickup if Achane's prognosis for Week 4 is iffy. -- Cockcroft

stories.headline: Columbus stuns Miami late after Messi's free-kick golazo
stories.summary: Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win over MLS Cup holders Inter Miami on Sunday.
stories.body:
Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win over MLS Cup holders Inter Miami on Sunday.

Ahead of his farewell to the Argentina national team, Lionel Messi continued to show he has plenty to offer by scoring a free kick from an improbable angle in the first half to seemingly give Miami a share of the points.

But just moments from the final whistle, and shortly after a red card for Miami substitute Santiago Morales, Columbus substitute Thiaré scored on the rebound after Miami goalkeeper Rocco Ríos Novo spilled a shot into his path.

The late drama overshadowed what was another memorable moment from Miami's No. 10.

Messi, 39, will play his final match in his national team's jersey when Argentina take on Benin in an Oct. 6 friendly at Buenos Aires' Monumental Stadium, following his announcement in late August that he was ending his international career.

But before heading to Argentina, he gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

The 33rd-minute effort was Messi's 12th direct free-kick goal for Inter Miami in all competitions and sixth this season. He now has 21 goals in MLS this year, extending his lead at the top of the Golden Boot race to three goals over FC Dallas' Petar Musa.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Miami had trailed for just five minutes in the first half, falling behind when its former striker Josef Martínez converted a penalty after he was fouled in the area by Yannick Bright.

But Columbus will likely feel the late win was justified after Anass Zaroury was denied by the woodwork on three separate occasions.

The result leaves Miami in third place in the Eastern Conference, level on points with second-placed New England Revolution and 14 points behind runaway leaders Nashville SC.

The win could be significant for Columbus, taking the team up to 12th in the East and keeping it in the running for a playoff spot.

stories.headline: 2026 MLB offseason manager changes: Tracking hirings, firings
stories.summary: The offseason carousel starts with an opening in Seattle. Here's who is out -- and who could be in line to replace them.
stories.body:
The first managerial change of the 2026-27 MLB offseason came Sunday when Dan Wilson told reporters he would not be returning as skipper of the Seattle Mariners.

The move came on the season's final day, as the Mariners finished out a once-hopeful 2026 campaign with a disappointing 76-86 record, finishing third in a weak American League West.

Which major league teams will change managers next? And who could be next in line?

ESPN will track all of the managerial hirings and firings -- and provide potential top replacements for every opening as they happen.

Seattle Mariners
2026 manager: Dan Wilson (Sept. 27)

Wilson is out in his second full season in Seattle after being hired in August 2024 to replace Scott Servais.

The Mariners entered the 2026 season as division favorites and a potential top American League contender coming off a 2025 playoff run that saw them eight outs away from the franchise's first World Series appearance before falling to the Toronto Blue Jays in Game 7 of the ALCS. Seattle got off to a slow start, with just four wins in its first 13 games. With season-long struggles from big stars like Cal Raleigh and Julio Rodriguez, coupled with inconsistent pitching and an underperforming offense, the Mariners never got to more than four games over .500 on the season.

"This season has been very difficult, and of course the results have not been what any of us had expected," Wilson said after Sunday's 7-3 win over the Angels. "As a result, it was concluded that today is my last day as manager of the Seattle Mariners."
